stories.headline: Pakistan's US-Iran mediation role collapses amid 'double-dealing' accusations as land routes to Iran open
stories.summary: Pakistan's bid to serve as the primary intermediary between the United States and Iran dominated the week's coverage. Asim Munir shuttled between Washington and Tehran contacts, Iran's FM Araghchi visited Islamabad twice for talks with PM Shehbaz and Munir, and a second round of US-Iran talks scheduled for Islamabad failed to materialise. Simultaneously, Islamabad formalised six overland transit routes for Iran-bound goods amid the US naval blockade of Hormuz, triggering widespread accusations that Pakistan was running a 'double game' — taking Saudi money to enforce Iran isolation while opening corridors that undercut US pressure. Iran subsequently sidelined Pakistan as mediator in favour of Oman; Trump reviewed but rejected Iran's 14-point peace proposal transmitted via Islamabad.

stories.headline: President Zardari attends Hangor-class submarine commissioning during five-day China visit
stories.summary: President Asif Ali Zardari completed a five-day official visit to China (April 25–May 1) that included attending the commissioning of Pakistan's first Hangor-class submarine in Sanya — described as a 'historic milestone' in naval modernisation — alongside naval chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf. The visit also produced a joint venture agreement and multiple MoUs covering construction machinery, animal vaccines, medical technology, and water cooperation, and included high-level meetings with provincial leaders in Hunan and Hainan focused on CPEC 2.0 expansion.

stories.headline: Imran Khan marks 1,000 days in jail amid health concerns, legal proceedings, and PTI protest plans
stories.summary: PTI founder Imran Khan reached the milestone of 1,000 days of imprisonment on approximately May 2, with his party condemning the detention as political victimisation. Reporting this week covered Khan's ongoing eye treatment at PIMS (fourth intravitreal injection), his humanitarian release petition to the Islamabad High Court citing 90% vision loss and solitary confinement, IHC hearings on his Al-Qadir Trust appeal and a petition to ban his X account, the UN Committee Against Torture raising alarm over his detention, PTI and allied groups announcing nationwide protests, and the government's adviser Rana Sanaullah denying any deal for Khan's release.

stories.headline: Pakistan-Afghanistan border conflict escalates with strikes, civilian deaths, and refugee flow
stories.summary: Cross-border violence between Pakistan and Afghanistan intensified across the week. Pakistani forces conducted strikes under 'Operation Ghazab lil-Haq' targeting Afghan Taliban and TTP positions in Chaman and Waziristan sectors; Afghanistan accused Pakistan of attacking Kunar University, killing at least seven; nine civilians were reportedly killed in Afghan shelling in Bajaur; ISPR announced 13 TTP militants killed in separate border infiltration attempts in Mohmand and North Waziristan; and hundreds of Afghan refugees were stranded at Torkham awaiting repatriation amid the fighting.

stories.headline: Pakistan's weekly oil import bill triples to $800m as US-Iran war batters economy
stories.summary: PM Shehbaz Sharif told cabinet that Pakistan's oil import bill had surged from $300 million to $800 million per week due to the US-Iran conflict's impact on global energy markets, acknowledging 'major economic fallout.' A minister separately admitted Pakistan holds only five to seven days of crude reserves — no strategic buffer comparable to India's — and economists warned of double-digit inflation. Shehbaz subsequently cut petrol prices by PKR 80 per litre but supply pressures persisted.

stories.headline: Marka-e-Haq first anniversary marked with military celebrations; India releases Operation Sindoor strike list
stories.summary: Pakistan held commemorative events marking the first anniversary of 'Marka-e-Haq' — the military's name for the May 2025 India-Pakistan aerial conflict — including an ISPR anthem release, rallies at Mazar-e-Quaid, and an AJK-declared 'Solidarity with Pakistan Army' week. Simultaneously, the Indian Army released a list of seven Pakistani terror camps targeted during Operation Sindoor and Indian analysts debated post-Sindoor military lessons, while Pakistani social media circulated a debunked fake video of an S-400 air defence system being destroyed.

stories.headline: Pakistan conducts Fateh-II missile training launch and three additional missile tests in April
stories.summary: Pakistan's Army Rocket Force Command conducted a training launch of the indigenously developed Fateh-II surface-to-surface guided missile system, with ISPR announcing successful validation of technical parameters, avionics, and navigation systems. Separate reporting noted two additional missile tests in April — the SMASH and Taimoor systems — bringing the April total to three tests. President Zardari, PM Shehbaz, and CDF Asim Munir praised the tests; Janes noted the launch likely signals the Fateh-II is entering operational deployment.

stories.headline: World Press Freedom Day: Zardari, Shehbaz, and Bilawal issue statements; CPNE elects new leadership
stories.summary: On World Press Freedom Day (May 3), President Zardari, PM Shehbaz Sharif, and PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari issued separate statements reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to media freedom, warning against disinformation, and paying tribute to journalists. Zardari also congratulated newly elected CPNE office-bearers. The statements came amid continued controversy over media suppression — opposition press conference criticism and the Islamabad press-meeting controversy earlier in the week undercut the official framing.
